When using parameters for the @o tag make sure to close the tag with ;(semicolon). In case of your grenade case you’d have to write @o throwables;. comments.author: Nightingale
comments.body_html:
You can write whatever you want in the tag name. As long as @sl/@ml/@o tag is present in the name and separated by spaces, the corresponding feature is going to work, which should be confirmed by a notification when you save the tag.

E.g. your tags can look like this:

- Ammo @ml @o n:!grenade;

- Food @o food;

- Drinks @o drinks;

Or even:

- I love @ml moving every @o info items|electronics; item manually

Of course having some readable text in the beginning is the most sensible, since that’s the part you should be able to see the most.

comments.author: Brin
comments.body_html:
Hopefully you’ve already figured this out by now, and this will just help the next person who has a similar issue.

You can filter items by name, or by category, but you need to get the syntax right. For dogtags, that would mean:

By category: “@o … !others”
By name: “@o … n:!dogtag”

Your sort tag didn’t work right because you told the mod to filter based on a category that doesn’t exist.
